newsitem.title: USA: Eaton to buy Fusion Systems for $39 per shr.
newsitem.headline: Eaton to buy Fusion Systems for $39 per shr.

text.p: Eaton Corp and Fusion Systems Corp said Monday they have a definitive agreement for Eaton to acquire Fusion Systems for $39 per share.
The companies said the deal calls for Eaton to initiate a cash tender offer for all outstanding Fusion shares at $39 per share by no later than July 7.
The tender offer will be subject to a majority of the outstanding Fusion shares on a fully diluted basis being tendered, and other customary conditions, the companies said.
Following the tender offer, Eaton will acquire remaining Fusion shares in a merger at the same $39 per share price.
Fusion Systems had approximately 7.5 million shares outstanding as of June 27, they said.

Fusion Systems also has declared a dividend of one contingent payment right on each Fusion share outstanding on July 25, they said. The contingent payment right entitles Fusion shareholders to receive on March 31, 1999, an additional cash payment if Fusion Systems' 1998 revenues exceed $122 million, with a maximum $5.00 per right payment made if Fusion's revenues are $149 million or more.
The contingent payment rights will expire on December 31, 1997, unless Eaton or another third party acquires control of Fusion by that date, they said.
Eaton chairman and chief executive officer Stephen Hardis said the merger is consistent with Eaton's growth strategy.

"We have set a growth goal for our semiconductor equipment business of $1.5 billion in sales in the next five years," Hardis said. "It is one of the major drivers for our overall corporate target of becoming a $10 billion company by the year 2000. The potential of Fusion Systems will be a significant factor in our semiconductor equipment growth plans."

Founded in 1971, Rockville, Md.-based Fusion is a supplier of front-end process equipment to the semiconductor industry, the companies said. It has about 400 employees and offices throughout the United States, Europe, Japan and Korea. Sales in 1996 were $84.6 million, more than half coming from Europe and Pacific Rim countries.
